nodes.label: JPL A-Team
nodes.rationale: Small, diverse team of experienced SMEs focused on systems engineering; rapidly and inexpensively explores design space for CML 1-3, using CML-appropriate tools whose fidelity matches the decision needed (e.g. CML 2 cost tool determines cost class).

nodes.label: CML 3 Trade Space
nodes.rationale: Trade space exploration increases likelihood of finding a global optimum; skipping it led to sub-maximal science return and inefficient spacecraft/ground designs.

nodes.label: CML Matrix
nodes.rationale: 7 columns (CML 1-7) by 24 rows binned as Science(2), Technical(13), Management(5), Cost(1), Other(3), aligned with how NASA evaluates concepts (science review then TMCO). Read down a column to see what a review needs, or across a row to see products over time.

nodes.label: CML Matrix Cost Row (Cost Estimation and Cost Risk)
nodes.norm_label: cml matrix cost row (cost estimation and cost risk)

nodes.label: CML Matrix Management Rows
nodes.rationale: Omitted programmatic portions can force a full redesign or unacceptable lifecycle cost growth.

nodes.label: CML Matrix Other Rows
nodes.rationale: Launch approval, NEPA and export compliance are often handled after the fact, causing cost growth or inability to implement the concept.

nodes.label: JPL Team X
nodes.rationale: Created 1995 for tighter budgets; initiated collaborative engineering at NASA; 1000+ studies; focuses on CML 4 point designs, typically 3 sessions over a week.

nodes.label: TMCO (Technical, Management, Cost and Other) Review
nodes.norm_label: tmco (technical, management, cost and other) review

nodes.label: CML 2-4 Iterative Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Mission design is not linear early on; looping between feasibility, trade space and point design lets teams return to earlier stages when problems arise. Presented as a strength, not a weakness.

nodes.label: Concept Maturity Level (CML)
nodes.rationale: Before CMLs there was no way to measure work placed in a concept, know when trade space exploration is most advantageous, compare concepts at equal maturity, or estimate work to the next level; CMLs give a standardized vocabulary for progress in Pre-Phase A.

nodes.label: BioNutrients Project
nodes.rationale: Need: rapid, safe, reliable in-place production of dietary nutrients with minimal mass, power and volume for long-duration missions, since stored food degrades.

nodes.label: BioNutrients-2
nodes.rationale: Goals: enable yeast growth, produce targeted beta carotene on ISS, reduce mass and volume vs BioNutrients-1.

nodes.label: Fluorinated Ethylene Propylene (FEP) Bag
nodes.rationale: Two thicknesses: 3 mil for yeast, 5 mil for yogurt/kefir.

nodes.label: Begin with the End in Mind
nodes.norm_label: begin with the end in mind
nodes.rationale: Requirements derive from the end product: the publication (type/quantity of data needed) and the demonstrated resource reduction drive sample quantity, repetition and quality.

nodes.label: Concept of Operations (ConOps)
nodes.rationale: Per NPR 7123.1: describes time-sequenced system use to meet stakeholder expectations, stimulates requirements and architecture, and provides validation criteria.

nodes.label: On-Console Scientist & Engineer Support
nodes.rationale: Scientists and engineers stay on console during operations in case of crew questions or anomalies.

nodes.label: BioNutrients-2 Resource Requirements
nodes.rationale: For same starting sample size as BioNutrients-1: <250 g sample container, <300 mL total occupied volume.

nodes.label: BioNutrients-2 Science Requirements
nodes.rationale: >=12 replicate samples, >=30 mL per sample, >=3 ug beta carotene/mL, >=1 mg dry cell weight per sample, no microbial contamination.

nodes.norm_label: space segment experiment procedure (hydrate, incubate, freeze)

nodes.norm_label: user segment sample processing (delivery, thaw, empty & wash, centrifuge, analyze)

nodes.label: Verification Planning During Requirements Definition
nodes.rationale: Plan how each requirement will be verified before implementation, e.g. <250 g container verified by weighing an empty container.

nodes.label: Ground Station
nodes.rationale: Inadequate ground station is a mission killer; build and test early, practice on existing satellites.

nodes.label: Launch
nodes.rationale: CubeSats have no influence on launch date; the LV leaves without a late CubeSat.

nodes.label: Dynamic Environment Testing
nodes.rationale: Shows survival of launch vibration/shock; no physical hardware changes allowed afterwards.

nodes.label: Launch Vehicle
nodes.rationale: Any rocket can carry CubeSats if it has performance margin, goes to the desired orbit, and can accept dispensers.

nodes.label: Outgassing
nodes.rationale: Use low-outgassing materials to possibly avoid thermal vacuum bakeout.

nodes.label: Thermal Vacuum Bakeout
nodes.rationale: Outgasses contaminants before launch to protect sensitive primary payloads.

nodes.label: Thermal Vacuum Cycling
nodes.rationale: Optional internal screening for thermal cycling damage; cannot replace bakeout.

nodes.label: CubeSat-to-Dispenser ICD
nodes.rationale: Encompasses most range safety requirements; the governing requirement set verified by all flight certification deliverables.

nodes.label: Mass Properties Report
nodes.rationale: Out-of-tolerance mass can lead to demanifesting because it creates unknown risk to the LV; include large but reasonable margins.

nodes.label: Venting Analysis
nodes.rationale: Rapid ascent pressure drop could burst trapped air pockets, endangering LV and other payloads.

nodes.label: Launch Services Program
nodes.rationale: Pairs selected CubeSats with launches; LSP-REQ-317.01 ensures CubeSats add no risk to primary payload.

nodes.label: Mission Integrator
nodes.rationale: Single party responsible for schedule, deliverables, ICD and communication between CubeSat developers and LV provider.

nodes.label: Interface Control Document
nodes.rationale: Official rulebook for the CubeSat; derived from CDS, dispenser-to-LV ICD, range safety and LV needs; specifies test levels.

nodes.label: Orbital Debris Assessment Report
nodes.rationale: NASA generates it for all CSLI CubeSats under every mission model.

nodes.label: CubeSat 101
nodes.rationale: Written for first-time CubeSat developers, especially at educational institutions, because little information exists for newcomers.

nodes.label: Exploration Mission (Presidential directive driven)
nodes.rationale: Science missions are driven by SMD strategic plans whereas exploration missions may be driven by Presidential directive.

nodes.label: Soft-Stowed Ambient-Temperature Launch
nodes.rationale: Samples launched at ambient temperature, protected from oxygen and moisture, avoiding powered cold stowage.

nodes.label: Amateur License
nodes.rationale: Simplest but hardest to qualify for: no Government or commercial involvement; FCC judges operator, NOAA judges owner; no encryption.

nodes.label: Experimental License
nodes.rationale: Typical license for university/CSLI CubeSats; must operate on non-interference basis and be able to cease emissions. FCC needs at least 90 days, so apply ASAP.

nodes.label: IARU
nodes.rationale: Volunteer body meeting periodically, so review cycles are slow; submit coordination requests immediately after manifesting.

nodes.label: Non-Earth Imaging Waiver
nodes.rationale: Adds significant time; updating an application to add one restarts the process.

nodes.label: Regulatory Licensing
nodes.rationale: Licensing is lengthy; apply within 30 days of manifesting or risk demanifest. An early CubeSat nearly had its release disabled for lacking an FCC license.

nodes.label: CubeSat
nodes.rationale: Standardized shape/size/mass lets vendors mass-produce COTS parts and lowers transport and deployment cost; begun 1999 to give universities affordable access to space.

nodes.label: CubeSat Unit (1U)
nodes.rationale: 1U is a 10 cm cube of about 1-1.33 kg; larger sizes 1.5U, 2U, 3U, 6U, 12U.

nodes.label: Dispenser
nodes.rationale: Interface between CubeSat and launch vehicle: attaches to LV, protects CubeSat during launch, releases it on command.

nodes.label: P-POD
nodes.rationale: First CubeSat dispenser (Poly-Picosatellite Orbital Deployer) from Cal Poly; holds 3U, door opens on LV electrical signal.

nodes.label: CubeSat Design Specification
nodes.rationale: General requirements for all CubeSats; useful for preliminary design but not the official launch requirements (the mission ICD is).

nodes.label: Free Advice Design Considerations
nodes.rationale: Keep it simple (CDS prohibits pyrotechnics, propulsion makes providers nervous); put key components on exterior for rework; do not design to envelope limits; double burn wires; use flight-heritage components; use UL listed batteries.

nodes.label: Keys to CSLI Selection
nodes.rationale: Adequate funding, strong merit and feasibility reviews, clear benefit to NASA.

nodes.label: NASA CSLI
nodes.rationale: NASA covers launch cost for qualified CubeSats (auxiliary payloads or ISS deployments) in exchange for a report on investigation results; enables low-cost public-private partnerships.

nodes.label: CubeSat Hardware Fabrication and Testing
nodes.rationale: Building two flight units plus ETU and FlatSat is cheaper than building another later and lets you fly the best hardware.

nodes.label: Development Testing
nodes.rationale: Test like you fly; test subsystems before integration.

nodes.label: Securing Funding
nodes.rationale: Developers pay all development/operations costs; running out of money can waste NASA sunk costs and demanifest co-manifested CubeSats, so do not accept a launch until confident of on-time delivery. Keep at least 10% reserves.

nodes.label: Technology Demonstration Missions
nodes.rationale: Agencies like JPL fly new components on cheap CubeSats to reduce risk to expensive satellite missions.

nodes.label: CRADA
nodes.rationale: Contract signed after manifesting; requires reimbursing NASA for integration and launch costs if the CubeSat is not delivered on time.

nodes.label: CML Checklists
nodes.rationale: Needed to quickly, repeatably measure maturity and show gaps. Generated only for CML 2-6: CML 1 is free-form, and CML 7+ is governed by NPR 7120.5E. Caveats: measures completeness not quality, no attribute weighting, self-assessment is overly optimistic so an independent assessor is needed.

nodes.label: Ground System / Mission Operations System Design
nodes.norm_label: ground system / mission operations system design

nodes.label: Technical Margins
nodes.rationale: CML 4 checklist margins: S/C dry mass >=35%, power >=35%, energy >=35%, flight software >=100%, telecom >=3 dB deep space / >=6 dB proximity; propellant, data storage and attitude control margins not required by the AO.

nodes.label: CML Matrix Technical Rows
nodes.rationale: Concurrent design of mission with spacecraft and ground systems as an integrated system.

nodes.label: Mission Complexity
nodes.rationale: Complexity strongly affects maturity, risk posture and lifecycle cost but is hard to assess in Pre-Phase A; future work plans to weight checklist elements and complexity.

nodes.label: RYG Status and 80% Maturity Threshold
nodes.rationale: Each attribute marked green/yellow/red; a concept is at a CML if 80% of attributes are green, but nothing is special about 80% and engineering judgment is required (e.g. missing Science Traceability Matrix outweighs percentage).
